top_jobs.job: When the weekly numbers land on Monday with spend up and revenue flat, help me know by noon which ad sets and placements to cut, hold or scale and by how much, so I stop the week's budget leaking into losers
top_jobs.metric: share of spend in ad sets above target cost per purchase after spending 3 times that target, 7 day click

top_jobs.job: When Meta shows a great week but the store orders and the bank do not agree, help me see what the ads really made and set how much a new customer may cost, so I do not scale on a number that is not real
top_jobs.metric: gap between Meta-reported purchases and store orders from paid social, and cost per new customer from store data

top_jobs.job: When revenue from ads looks strong but new customers are flat, help me move spend toward people who have never bought, at the right awareness level and in the segments that buy, so I grow the customer base instead of paying for repeat orders
top_jobs.metric: new customers per week from paid social, and share of spend reaching past buyers

top_jobs.job: When new ads, creators or a new product go live next week, help me check every link and rule before spend starts and set each test up to end with a clear yes or no, so I do not waste launch day or pay for tests that end with not sure
top_jobs.metric: share of tests read as a clear win or loss, and launch-day errors

top_jobs.job: When a best seller has 10 days of stock left, a sale is coming, or slow stock ties up cash, help me move spend to what we can ship and plan the ramp and the stop, so I do not pay for buyers who cannot buy
top_jobs.metric: ad spend on products with under 14 days of stock

jobs.job: Rank every ad set each Monday by dollars spent above target, and mark each cut, hold or scale with a dollar amount, judging only ad sets that spent at least 3 times target cost per purchase
jobs.trigger: every Monday by 10am, and any day spend jumps 20 percent

inputs.need: ad set spend, purchases and value, 7 and 28 days, 7 day click
target cost per purchase per product from margin
approval rules: what a buyer may change without the founder
the creative verdicts for the same week

steps: Compute in code per ad set: spend, purchases, cost per purchase, dollars above target
Put ad sets under 3 times target spend in 'not read yet'
Cut: over 1.5 times target for 7 days. Scale: under target for 7 days. Hold: the rest
Write the dollar change for each: cut to zero, hold, or raise by the step in 11-03
Mark changes that need the founder under the approval rules
Log every call with the reason so next Monday can check it
jobs.output: a Monday list: every ad set with cut, hold, scale or not read yet, the dollar change and the reason

watch.metric: share of spend in ad sets above target after 3 times target spend

jobs.drives: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.job: Tell the buyer for each new ad after 2 days whether to kill it or wait, by showing how far it is from the read spend and whether its hook and click rate are already below the kill line
jobs.trigger: daily for ads launched in the last 7 days

inputs.need: daily ad-level spend, impressions, 3 second views, clicks, purchases
account medians for hook rate and click rate
target cost per purchase

steps: Show each new ad's spend as a share of 3 times target
Kill early only if hook rate is under half the account median after 2,000 impressions
Otherwise wait, and show the date it will reach read spend at the current pace
If it will never reach read spend, flag the budget, not the ad
jobs.output: a daily new ad list: kill, wait with a read date, or budget too small

watch.metric: share of killed ads that had reached read spend

jobs.job: Raise the budget of each ad set that beat target for 7 days in steps sized to its read window, check cost per purchase after each step, and step back if it breaks
jobs.trigger: when 11-01 marks an ad set scale

inputs.need: ad set daily spend and cost per purchase, 14 days
the ceiling on cost per new customer
monthly budget cap

steps: Set the step so the ad set can spend 3 times target in the next read window
Raise once, then wait for the read window before the next step
After each step, compare cost per purchase with the ceiling
Step back to the last good budget if it goes over the ceiling for 3 days
Fork new creative into a new ad set; never edit the winning ad set's ads
jobs.output: a scale log per ad set: each step, its date and cost per purchase after it

watch.metric: cost per purchase in the 7 days after each budget step

jobs.drives: new customers per week at or under the ceiling

jobs.job: Break every cut ad set's spend down by age, gender, placement and region, find the cells that still bought near target, and relaunch the best creative only in those cells with a capped budget
jobs.trigger: every Monday, for ad sets marked cut

inputs.need: breakdowns by age, gender, placement and region with spend and purchases
postmortem of the ads in the set
target cost per purchase

steps: Lay out a grid of spend and cost per purchase by age and gender, then by placement
Mark cells under target with at least 10 purchases
Mark cells that took over 20 percent of spend with no purchases
Relaunch the ad in the good cells with a new first frame if the postmortem says hook
Cap the relaunch at 3 times target and read it like a new test
jobs.output: a segment grid per cut ad set and a capped relaunch in the cells that bought

watch.metric: cost per purchase of relaunched ad sets

jobs.job: Read spend and purchases by placement over 28 days, and remove placements that take over 5 percent of spend with cost per purchase above 2 times target
jobs.trigger: on the 1st of each month

inputs.need: placement breakdown with spend, purchases and value, 28 days
TikTok placement report, when the brand runs TikTok
target cost per purchase

steps: Compute in code cost per purchase and share of spend per placement
Flag placements over 5 percent of spend at over 2 times target
Check the ads there have a format made for that placement before removing it
Exclude the placement or make a format for it, and log which
Recheck in 28 days
jobs.output: a placement table with the placements removed or given their own format
jobs.next: feeds 09-10 (formats for placements that should work)

watch.metric: share of spend in placements over 2 times target

jobs.job: Compare Meta-reported purchases and value with store orders from paid social each week, per campaign, and show the gap and the store-side cost per new customer
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and before any budget raise over 20 percent

inputs.need: Meta purchases and value by campaign, 7 day click and 1 day view split
orders with UTMs, new or returning, and gross profit
sessions by source and campaign
numbers not to trust and since when

steps: Match store orders to campaigns by UTM; count new customers apart from repeat buyers
Put Meta purchases next to store orders per campaign and compute the gap in percent
Show 1 day view purchases as a separate column, not added in
Compute store-side cost per new customer and marketing efficiency (store revenue divided by total ad spend)
If the gap moves over 20 points in a week, flag tracking to 22-measurement
jobs.output: a weekly table per campaign: Meta purchases, store orders, gap, new customers and store-side cost per new customer

watch.metric: gap between Meta purchases and store orders from paid social

jobs.drives: budget decisions made on store numbers

jobs.job: Set the most a new customer may cost for each product line from first order gross profit and 12 month repeat buying, and put it in every scale and cut rule
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then each quarter or after a price change

inputs.need: orders with product, discount, shipping and returns, 12 months
landed cost per SKU
how long the founder can wait to earn back a customer

steps: Compute gross profit on the first order per product line
Compute repeat gross profit per customer at 90 days and 12 months by first product
Set two ceilings: break even on the first order, and break even within the founder's payback window
Founder picks one per line and signs it
Write the ceilings into the finance shelf and into 11-01 and 11-03
jobs.output: a signed ceiling for cost per new customer per product line

watch.metric: share of spend in ad sets above their line's ceiling

jobs.job: Split each product's revenue from ads by gross margin and set a return on spend target per product, so low margin products stop getting the same target as high margin ones
jobs.trigger: once a quarter, and when catalog ads run over 30 percent of spend

inputs.need: product-level ad spend and value, including catalog ads
gross margin per product
product sets in the catalog

steps: Compute in code break even return on spend per product: 1 divided by gross margin
Group products into 3 margin bands
Build a product set per band and give each its own target
Show spend share per band before and after
jobs.output: a target per margin band and the catalog split into 3 product sets

watch.metric: share of spend on the low margin band

jobs.job: Check the agency's changes each month against store profit: list every budget, audience and ad change from the account log and what cost per new customer did in the 14 days after
jobs.trigger: on the 3rd of each month, before the agency call

inputs.need: account activity log of changes
store-side cost per new customer by week
the agency's monthly report and fee

steps: Pull every change with its date and who made it
Group into budget, audience, ad and setting changes
Show store-side cost per new customer 14 days before and after each group
Compare with what the report claims
Write 3 questions for the agency call
jobs.output: a monthly change log with before and after store numbers and 3 questions for the agency

watch.metric: store-side cost per new customer month on month

jobs.job: Split spend each week into prospecting, retargeting and past buyers, show how much reaches people who already bought, and exclude recent buyers from every cold campaign
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and when new customers are flat 2 weeks while revenue rises

inputs.need: campaigns, ad sets and audiences with spend
new vs returning orders by campaign
customer list for exclusions, refreshed weekly
the repurchase cycle per product

steps: Label each ad set prospecting, retargeting or past buyers
Compute spend share and new customer share per label
Find the share of cold ad set purchases that were returning customers
Add or refresh the buyer exclusion, sized to the repurchase cycle
Keep past buyer spend in one campaign so it cannot bleed into cold
jobs.output: a funnel split: spend and new customers per stage, and exclusions in place

watch.metric: share of cold purchases from returning customers

jobs.job: Move 15 percent of prospecting spend to unaware and problem aware ads for 4 weeks as a test, reading new customers and store-side cost per new customer against the old split
jobs.trigger: when the heat map shows under 20 percent of spend on unaware and problem aware ads

inputs.need: the heat map and gap line
at least 4 live top of funnel ads from the 09-12 briefs
new customer orders by week
founder sign-off on a 4 week test

steps: Read spend share and cost per new customer by awareness level from the heat map
Put the top of funnel ads in their own ad set with 15 percent of prospecting budget
Point them to pages at the same level, not the checkout
Read weekly on new customers and store-side cost per new customer, not on last click return
At 4 weeks, keep, grow or roll back, and log it in the ledger
jobs.output: a 4 week budget test with a keep, grow or roll back call
jobs.next: feeds 09-06 (T0 rule on awareness mix) and 22-measurement

watch.metric: share of spend on unaware and problem aware ads

jobs.drives: new customers per week and cost per new customer

jobs.job: Give the 2 best segments by age, gender and placement their own ads written for them, and list the segments with high reach where no ad speaks to them
jobs.trigger: every other Monday

inputs.need: breakdowns by age, gender, placement and region, 28 days
copy sets written for each segment cell (10-04)
avatars and share of orders per avatar

steps: Rank segment cells by cost per new customer, with at least 30 purchases
Add the tailored copy and creative for the top 2 cells to the live broad ad set, not a narrow one
List cells with over 10 percent of reach and under half their share of purchases
Send those cells to 10-copy as the next brief
Compare cost per purchase in each cell before and after 14 days
jobs.output: tailored ads live for the 2 best cells and a list of cells nobody speaks to

watch.metric: cost per purchase in the top 2 segment cells

jobs.job: Each month, launch the 10 search-sourced hooks as a Meta test, and send the 3 Meta angles with the lowest cost per new customer to Google Ads and the SEO list
jobs.trigger: on the 1st of each month, after the bridge sheet is written

inputs.need: the monthly bridge sheet
Meta angles with store-side cost per new customer
Google search terms and Amazon review phrases

steps: Launch the 10 search-sourced hooks in one ad set on the best performing body
Read at 3 times target spend and keep the hooks that beat the account median
Send the 3 best Meta angles to 12-google-ads as headline tests and to 17-seo as article topics
Log each line's source and result so the bridge learns which source works
jobs.output: one Meta test of search-sourced hooks and 3 angles handed to Google and SEO

watch.metric: hit rate of search-sourced hooks vs other hooks

jobs.drives: cost per new customer across channels

jobs.job: Check every ad in tomorrow's launch before spend starts: the link opens and has UTMs, the pixel fires, the product is in stock, the offer is live, the claims passed and the rights are valid
jobs.trigger: the day before every launch

inputs.need: ads in draft with URLs and UTMs
stock per product
pixel and conversion API event health
claim check results and rights end dates

steps: Open each URL on a phone and check it loads the right product or page
Check UTMs follow the naming rule
Check the purchase event fired in the last 24 hours with value
Check each product has over 14 days of stock and each offer is live in the store
Check claims passed 10-07 and rights run past 30 days
Return a pass or a list of fixes; nothing launches with a fail
jobs.output: a launch sheet with pass or fix per ad, signed before launch

watch.metric: ads launched with a broken link, no stock or a failed claim

jobs.job: Launch each creative test, such as the weekly AI video stack, as one ad set per concept with the winner line and read date written first, cap each ad's share, and log the result as a win, a loss or not tested
jobs.trigger: every launch, and every Tuesday for the AI video stack

inputs.need: the 3 picked cuts or variants
target cost per purchase and budget
the testing campaign
past test results

steps: Write the winner line before launch, e.g. 'under $32 per purchase at $96 spend'
Put the concept in its own ad set in the testing campaign, never in scaling
Set the budget so each ad can reach 3 times target in 7 days
Read on the read date; under read spend is logged as not tested
Move winners to the scaling campaign as a new ad set; log losers with a fail note
Note which cut length won, 15, 30 or 30 to 45 seconds
jobs.output: a launched test with a written winner line, a read date and a logged result

watch.metric: share of tests read as a clear win or loss

jobs.job: Run the best creator videos as partnership ads through the creator's handle, and compare cost per purchase with the same video run from the brand's handle
jobs.trigger: when a creator video beats the account median hook rate, and monthly

inputs.need: partnership ad permission from each creator
creator ranking by purchases
the video, run from the brand handle, with results
rights end dates

steps: Pick the 3 creator videos with the best purchases per 1,000 views
Request partnership access on each creator's handle
Launch each video twice in one ad set: creator handle and brand handle
Read both at 3 times target spend
Keep the handle that wins and put it in the creator's record
jobs.output: 3 handle tests with a result per creator, logged on the roster

watch.metric: cost per purchase of creator handle vs brand handle

jobs.drives: cost per new customer from creator content

jobs.job: Test the top ad sending to a page that repeats its promise against the same ad sending to the product page, split 50 and 50, for 14 days
jobs.trigger: when 10-11 scores a top 10 ad 1 or less for match

inputs.need: the match scores for the top 10 ads
a page built to repeat the ad's promise
inputs.from: page builder in the store theme

inputs.need: page conversion by ad

steps: Duplicate the ad with the new URL into the same ad set
Split budget evenly and cap each ad's share
Read cost per purchase and page conversion on each URL at 14 days
Keep the winner; if the matched page wins, add the rule to T0 and brief pages for the next 3 ads
jobs.output: a page test result for the top ad and a rule on which page each ad type should send to

watch.metric: conversion rate of paid sessions on the tested page

jobs.drives: cost per purchase on the top ad

jobs.job: Each morning, list products with under 14 days of stock and the ad spend behind them, move that spend to products that can ship, and plan the restart for when stock returns
jobs.trigger: daily

inputs.need: stock per SKU and sales per day, 28 days
ad spend by product, including catalog ads
incoming stock dates

steps: Compute days of stock per SKU in code: units on hand divided by sales per day
List SKUs under 14 days with the ad spend and ads behind them
Propose moving the spend to the nearest product with over 45 days of stock
Pull the SKU from catalog product sets when it is under 5 days
When stock lands, restart the paused ads in their old ad sets and watch cost for 3 days
jobs.output: a daily stock and spend list with the moves to make and a restart plan

watch.metric: ad spend on SKUs with under 14 days of stock

jobs.job: Plan each peak sale 3 weeks out: the budget ramp by day, the ads ready and tested, the stop date, and the cut-back the morning after the sale ends
jobs.trigger: 3 weeks before each peak on the calendar

inputs.need: peak dates and what went wrong last year
last year's daily spend and cost per purchase in the same weeks
the sale offer and its end time
stock for the sale products

steps: Set a daily budget curve: warm up 10 to 14 days before, peak on sale days, stop at the end time
Test sale ads 2 weeks before so winners are known on day 1
Grow the retargeting and email lists in the warm up weeks
Check stock covers the planned orders at the ramp budget
Schedule the cut-back for the morning after and the sale line sweep
jobs.output: a dated peak plan: budget per day, ads ready, stock check and the stop date

watch.metric: cost per purchase in the sale week vs plan

jobs.job: Point a capped share of spend at slow stock with a bundle or clearance ad, and stop when margin per order falls below the floor or stock reaches 60 days of cover
jobs.trigger: when a SKU has over 180 days of stock

inputs.need: days of stock per SKU
margin per order and the floor
a bundle or clearance offer the founder approves

steps: List SKUs with over 180 days of stock and the cash tied in each
Build a bundle with a best seller, or a clearance offer inside the discount floor
Run it in its own ad set capped at 10 percent of spend
Stop at the margin floor or 60 days of cover
Report cash freed and gross profit per order
jobs.output: a capped slow stock campaign with cash freed and margin per order tracked

watch.metric: units sold of the slow SKUs per week

new_enablers.name: Cut, hold and scale rules
new_enablers.what: Written rules computed in code for every ad set and ad: the read spend (3 times target) before any call, the kill, hold and scale lines, budget steps sized to the read window, and the approval line for the founder. Logs every call and its outcome.
inputs: target and ceiling cost per new customer
powers: Monday cut, hold and scale list
kill or wait on new ads
tests that end with an answer
peak ramps with a stop date

new_enablers.name: Launch preflight
new_enablers.what: Checks every ad before spend starts: the URL loads on a phone, UTMs follow the naming rule, the purchase event fires with value, the product has stock, the offer is live, claims passed and rights are valid. Returns pass or a fix list.
powers: no ads for sold out products

new_enablers.name: Ad and stock link
new_enablers.what: Joins days of stock per SKU with the ad spend and ads behind each SKU, so spend moves off products about to sell out, restarts when stock lands, and is pointed at slow stock inside a margin floor.
inputs: ad spend by product and catalog set
powers: no ads for products we cannot ship
